leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations contain B027 (GLP-1 and incretin therapies) as the single prize part, and all six cite the arc from hormone physiology to drugs with outcome-trial evidence. They do not share the laureate set: five members (El-Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius) name Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, while Linnarsson alone names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen. Citations differ accordingly, from a discovery-side wording about the physiology and active peptide to Linnarsson's wording about translation into therapies. Several members make their support for Mojsov conditional on a priority review, and Perlmann names a two-name Drucker and Holst fallback.

areas_of_agreement: B027 is the only ballot in any of the six preferred configurations, and no member proposes a second prize part.
Drucker and Holst are named by all six members, and no member disputes their roles.

Mechanism maturity and independent confirmation for B027 are not contested: members cite more than two decades of replication and randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease.

Members agree that attribution, not scientific merit, is the weak point of B027, and that Habener's absence from the credited list and the disputed priority for GLP-1(7-36) are unresolved from the supplied material.

For the alternatives, members agree that B015 (optogenetics) has high impact but a six-name credit that does not fit three places, and that B014 (unfolded protein response) has the cleanest two-name attribution.
scientific_disputes: Whether the prize should reward the physiology and identification of the active peptide (discovery-side trio) or a physiology-to-medicine arc that includes long-acting analogue design. Wahren-Herlenius and Perlmann treat analogue design as industrial or built on others' foundations, while Linnarsson treats the acylation and half-life solution as itself a discovery.

Whether a tool such as optogenetics (B015) ranks as a discovery with changed understanding or mainly changed experimental practice. Perlmann doubts that tool status is enough, while El-Manira and Svenningsson see no demerit in it.

Whether the unfolded protein response (B014) is held back by its largely mechanistic medical consequence. Wahren-Herlenius and Linnarsson reflect on this, while Perlmann and Svenningsson see it as a mature and clean basic-science alternative.

Whether TNF blockade (B006) rests on a clinical-translation claim only, because the underlying cytokine biology lies outside the supplied credit. El-Manira asked whether that gap is real, and Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius treat it as a weakness.
attribution_disputes: The third B027 laureate: Mojsov (five members) versus Knudsen (Linnarsson). Linnarsson regards Mojsov as the most contested name and Knudsen as the stronger name for the clinical step; the five Mojsov supporters regard Mojsov's identification and synthesis of GLP-1(7-36) as the necessary foundation.

Mojsov's priority relative to Habener, who is not on the credited list, cannot be settled from the supplied evidence according to several members. Linnarsson cautions that this priority question also affects peptide characterization.

Whether a contested priority claim should count against a candidate. Sandberg and Perlmann say contested priority is not a negative finding, while Linnarsson and others think it makes Mojsov the least secure of the credited names.

For B015, there is no agreed trio among Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth, Hegemann, Miesenboeck and Nagel. El-Manira, Perlmann and Svenningsson cite different trios from Nagel, Hegemann, Deisseroth and Bamberg, and members note that Boyden, Miesenboeck and Bamberg have claims that a three-person cap cannot absorb.

For B041 (CAR-T) and B011 (imatinib), members flag that foundational contributors are outside the credited names (Eshhar for CAR-T; the BCR-ABL and Philadelphia chromosome discoverers for imatinib), which weakens the credit as supplied.
maturity_disputes: B027 is described as mature, with several members calling recognition arguably overdue. Linnarsson raises the counterpoint that the therapeutic story is still expanding into cardiovascular, renal and neurological indications, and Wahren-Herlenius notes that long-term safety beyond metabolic disease is still being defined.
B041 (CAR-T) is questioned for unsettled solid-tumour results, long-term safety and the early autoimmune extension. B010 (cGAS-STING) has no approved therapy according to Wahren-Herlenius.

B014 (unfolded protein response) is mature in mechanism, with about thirty years of confirmation, but is questioned for indirect medical impact. Whether the line between it and the integrated stress response affects the citation (Ron, Kaufman) is open.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) has roughly twenty co-authored works with Perlmann, who ranks B014 and B010 as alternatives. Svenningsson also lists B014 as an alternative. Both state that this does not concern the credited candidates' own work, and no member claims a conflict with any credited name.

El-Manira discloses a 2009 paper with Perlmann, a 2019 review with Grillner and work with Ernfors, none of whom is credited. El-Manira also notes that optogenetics is a method in his own field, with no documented tie to any credited candidate.

Sandberg discloses topical proximity to the SMN2 splicing candidate (B016) and has not made it a preferred or alternative choice. Linnarsson discloses eight co-authored works with Sandberg, unconnected to the shortlisted discoveries.
Wahren-Herlenius discloses that TNF blockade (B006) lies in her own field of rheumatology and holds it only as an alternative, with no documented tie to Feldmann or Maini.
Perlmann notes that his profile does not establish the voting status of the Secretary-General.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee state, from documentary evidence rather than recollection, whether Mojsov's contribution (identification and synthesis of GLP-1(7-36)) is independent and prior enough to be credited, and how Habener's work bears on it?
If the priority question cannot be resolved, is the fallback a Drucker, Holst and Knudsen trio, a two-name Drucker and Holst prize, or a different configuration, and who decides?
Is the B027 citation meant to honour the physiology and active peptide, or the physiology-to-medicine arc including long-acting analogue design? Which citation wording follows from the answer?

Should any second prize part be considered at all given the three-person cap, and if so, which of B014, B015, B041 or B006 can be given a three-name or smaller credit that withstands attribution scrutiny?

For B015, can any trio be defended among Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth, Hegemann, Miesenboeck and Nagel, and does the channelrhodopsin discovery separate from its neuronal application in a way that supports a citation?
Does the absence from the credited names of upstream contributors (Eshhar for B041, TNF cloning for B006, the oncogene discoverers for B011) disqualify those candidates, or is it a framing matter?

The opening ranks quoted in several responses differ between members' accounts (for example the rank given to CAR-T, TNF blockade or optogenetics). Should round 2 rely only on the validated opening and shortlist files for ranks?
summary.chair_observation: B027 is the only ballot in any member's preferred configuration, with all six supporting it as the sole prize part, so the open question is the composition and wording rather than the choice. Five members name Drucker, Holst and Mojsov and one names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, and the stated disagreement is about the priority record for GLP-1(7-36) and about whether the prize honours physiology or the resulting medicines. Alternatives are scattered (B015 and B014 are each named by several members, B041, B006 and B010 by one or two) and none has a settled credit. This summary counts only positions explicit in the six round-1 files and is not a ruling.
